title: Mara and the Echo
premise: Ansel Dravenmoor is a clone of the murdered terraforming architect Elias Dravenmoor, and the colony's AI courts ruled he must inherit both the estate and the unsolved case. When every child on Halcyon Station begins dreaming the same dream — a voice counting down from a buried vault — Ansel discovers the original hid a failsafe: only half the cryosleep colonists can be revived before the station's failing reactor kills the rest. The dream is the original's dead lover, Dr. Mara Voss, still half-alive in the vault's neural archive, guiding the children toward a third option. To unlock it, Ansel must find who killed Elias — his own benefactor, Warden Ilsa Kettering, who feared Elias would wake Mara instead of her frozen daughter — and choose between duty to the colony's law and love for a woman made of echoes. In the end, Ansel sacrifices his own legal personhood to merge the archive with the reactor core, waking everyone at reduced odds, while Mara's consciousness survives in the dreams of the children who refuse to let her go.
about_author: Tamsin Zhou is a former orbital logistics dispatcher who wrote her first stories during long shifts monitoring cargo drones over the Pacific. She lives in Vancouver with her partner and an aging robot vacuum she insists has a personality.

chapters.title: Cargo of the Dead Man
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ten years after inheriting Elias's name, face, and murder case, Ansel hauls freight through contested orbits and endures casual cruelty from colonists who see him as a copy. He receives a court summons: the estate vault beneath the station will unseal in thirty days. Emotional beat: weary resignation hardening into reluctant curiosity.

chapters.title: The Children Who Dream Together
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Junie Okonkwo, an eight-year-old whose shared dream with forty other children draws colony-wide panic. She describes a woman's voice counting down inside a metal flower. The medics call it mass hysteria; Junie calls it Mara. Emotional beat: eerie wonder undercut by adult fear.

chapters.title: Inheritance of Enemies
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. At the summons hearing, Warden Ilsa Kettering — Elias's old friend and Ansel's legal guardian — urges him to void the inheritance. Ansel descends into the vault alone and finds Elias's final recording: 'If you're watching, you already dream of her.' Emotional beat: dread mixed with the first thrill of purpose.

chapters.title: A Voice Made of Light
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. The children sneak to the vault's outer hatch; Junie touches it and Mara speaks through her — a fragment of Dr. Mara Voss, archived mid-death ten years ago. Security drags the children away, but Junie carries a message for Ansel: 'He lied to protect you.' Emotional beat: awe curdling into danger.

chapters.title: The Reactor's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Decoding Elias's hidden files, Ansel learns the truth: the reactor can revive only half the twelve thousand sleepers before total failure. Elias built a third path with Mara — unfinished because someone killed him. Kettering's signature appears on the reactor logs. Emotional beat: betrayal blooming in slow motion.

chapters.title: What the Warden Buried
chapters.summary: Kettering's POV, first time. Flashbacks braid with present: she loved Elias, watched him choose Mara, and when Mara's shuttle 'failed,' Kettering silenced Elias to protect her own frozen daughter's priority slot. Now she must stop Ansel before the children wake something worse. Emotional beat: guilt weaponized into resolve.

chapters.title: Dreaming in Relay
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. Quarantined with the other children, Junie learns they can pass messages through the dream itself — Mara teaches them, one image per night. They map the vault's inner door for Ansel smuggled in crayon drawings. Emotional beat: solidarity and quiet courage.

chapters.title: The Counting Down
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Guided by the children's maps, Ansel breaches the vault and meets Mara's archive face to face — she mistakes him for Elias, then grieves him all over again. Kettering seals the vault behind them with the reactor at four days. Emotional beat: tender, impossible reunion shadowed by entrapment.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Alternating Ansel/Mara POV. Trapped together, they finish Elias's third path: merging the archive into the reactor core so revival runs on distributed consciousness — but it requires a legal person as anchor, and Ansel is the only clone eligible. Mara begs him not to; the children outside riot against Kettering. Emotional beat: the choice crystallizing.

chapters.title: Everyone Wakes
chapters.summary: Climax and resolution, ensemble POV. Ansel signs away his personhood and anchors the merge as Kettering, broken by her daughter's own recorded plea, unlocks the vault. Twelve thousand sleepers wake at reduced odds; Ansel dissolves into the core — except the children keep dreaming him, and Junie swears the voice now counts up. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into found family and enduring echo.
